title: Container Isolation Strength Comparator
description: Interactive p5.js simulator that runs five threat scenarios against chroot, default Docker, hardened Docker, a KVM virtual machine, and a confidential VM, badges each as blocked, mitigated with caveats, or feasible, and gives a verdict on whether the isolation level suits the chosen workload.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: cybersecurity
chapter_title: "System Security: OS, Memory, and Access Control"

educational.topic: Container and virtual machine isolation strength
learningObjectives: Evaluate whether a chosen isolation level mitigates host filesystem access, kernel exploitation, cache side channels, metadata-service access, and orchestrator API abuse.
Judge whether an isolation level is too weak, appropriate, or more than needed for a trusted, semi-trusted, or hostile multi-tenant workload.
Justify each mitigation using namespaces, capabilities, seccomp, MAC profiles, or hardware-assisted virtualization.
Recognize threats that isolation alone cannot stop and name the control layer that does.
educational.prerequisites: Namespaces, cgroups, capabilities, seccomp, MAC profiles, and the hypervisor trust boundary from the chapter.

pedagogical.modelType: judge-then-reveal evaluation tool driven by a threat-mitigation matrix
pedagogical.assessment: Students find the lightest isolation level that earns an Appropriate verdict for each workload and justify it from the rationale text.
misconceptionsAddressed: Believing a container is a security boundary equivalent to a virtual machine.
Assuming stronger isolation mitigates every threat, including network and API-authorization threats.
Assuming confidential computing protects the host from a hostile workload.

controls.label: Run threat suite
controls.action: evaluates the five threats and reveals the badges and verdict

controls.label: Reset
controls.action: restores Docker (default) with a fully trusted workload

model.assumptions: Each isolation level maps to a fixed status for each of five threats, stored in data.json. Each workload states the minimum status it requires per threat; the verdict compares the two and finds the lightest level that satisfies the workload.
model.limitations: A qualitative teaching matrix, not a measurement. Real outcomes depend on kernel version, runtime configuration, cloud settings such as the metadata hop limit, and controls outside the isolation boundary.
